flaws: Floating backboard: In the close-up view, the orange/brown backboard behind the white cup is completely floating in mid-air with no support structure attaching it to the desk, the cup base, or the ramp.

Non-functional decorative ring: In the low and top views, there is a brass ring mounted on a post in the middle of the track that is oriented parallel to the ramp off to the side, rather than spanning across the track for the marble to pass through.

Track overhangs the desk edge: In the top-down view, the upper-left starting section of the ramp and its first set of support pillars extend past the left boundary of the desk surface, nearly floating off the edge.

Crude end-of-track transitions: The two blue side blocks at the very end of the chute clip awkwardly into the rim of the white cup, and the stepped joints between the three ramp segments lack smooth brackets or visual joinery.
parsed.summary: Mechanically, the marble run is rock-solid, achieving 16/16 successful trials with a clean, well-contained trajectory. Visually, the color palette and desk props (lamp, books, succulent, spare marbles) establish a nice desk-toy theme, but floating geometry (especially the catch-cup backboard), the overhanging start tower, and the misaligned decorative ring keep it from looking like a truly polished physical product.
